page.layout: One page of text, one column. Above it a woodcut ornament band (not text). Title lines at the top, then a large woodcut initial A beginning the text, running text to the right of and below it. No margin notes, no running head, no catchword, no page number printed.

main_text.head: IOHANNES DRVSIVS, Lectori candido.
main_text.p: ANNI sunt sedecim plus minus, candide lector, cum hanc historiam auditoribus meis publice enarrare. Quo tempore nonnulla observavi quae digna luce videbantur hominibus minime invidis, cujusmodi paucos fert haec aetas. Nolui tamen ea publicare ob certas causas. Superiore anno cum affulgeret benignius astrum abOrdinum Delegatis hujus provinciae

page.notes: The first word is a large woodcut initial "A" joined to the following word: the printed text reads "ANNI" after the initial, so it is transcribed as "ANNI" (the initial is the first letter of "Anni"). The title line "IOHANNES DRVSIVS," and "Lectori candido." are set in spaced capitals and italic; the second line is italic and is treated as a heading. The word "hujus" and "provinciae" are followed by a printed "ciæ" at the line end, which is the continuation "ciae" of "provinciae" split across the line; the printed line ends with "ciæ" as shown. "abOrdinum" appears as printed with a capital O mid-word and "Delegatis" with a swash D; these are printing features and are left as printed. The text "minimeinvidis" in the scan is printed with a missing space, and "eapublicare" is printed as "ea publicare" in the scan with a space; spacing is not reproduced exactly.
